title: A Multi-center, Double-Blind, Randomized, Two-Arm, Parallel-Group, Placebo Controlled Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of ELGN-2112 on Intestinal Malabsorption in Preterm Infants
official: A Multi-center, Double-Blind, Randomized, Two-Arm, Parallel-Group, Placebo Controlled Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of ELGN-2112 on Intestinal Malabsorption in Preterm Infants
summary:
Main objective: To assess the efficacy of ELGN-2112 as compared to placebo on intestinal malabsorption in preterm infants as measured by number of days to achieve full enteral feeding*. 

*Defined as first day of reaching three consecutive days of EN feeds ≥150 ml/kg/day.

interventions.name: Powder for reconstitution for enteral administration

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Male or female preterm infants born at a gestational age 26+0 to 31+6 weeks. Gestational age matching (±2 weeks) between maternal dates and/or early antenatal ultrasound
2. Infant is cardiovascularly stable at time of enrolment and would be considered unstable if they require inotropic support
3. Infant is able to tolerate enteral feeds (defined as minimum of 10 ml/kg/day)
4. Infant is expected to wean off parenteral nutrition (PN) at the primary hospital
5. Informed consent form signed by parent(s) or legal guardian
6. In the Investigator’s opinion, the infant is sufficiently stable to partake in the trial to completion
7. (France only) - only participants benefiting from a health insurance plan can participate in research
8. Birth weight ≥ 500 g
9. Singleton or twin birth
10. Postnatal age up through and including Day 5 (up to 120 hours post birth)
11. Fraction of inspired oxygen ≤ 0.60 at enrolment
Exclusion criteria:
1. Infant is consuming more than 80 ml/kg/day enterally at study entry
2. Maternal diabetes (Type I/II or gestational) requiring insulin during pregnancy or in mothers past medical history
3. Confirmed hyperinsulinemia or suspected hyperinsulinemia requiring glucose administration of more than 12 mg/kg/min at randomization
4. Any systemic insulin administration at randomization
5. Nothing per os (NPO) at study entry and enteral/oral supplements are not allowed
6. Hypersensitivity to any of the drug components- Recombinant Human Insulin (rh-Insulin), Maltodextrin, Sodium Chloride
7. Infant is receiving pharmacological treatment for a hemodynamically significant PDA at the time of randomization
8. Heart and chest compression or any resuscitation drugs given to the infant during delivery
9. Subjects at risk for significant GI complications such as twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS) or monochorionic monoamniotic twins
10. Participation in another interventional clinical study that may interfere with the results of this trial
11. Infant is not dependent on any parenteral amino acids/lipids as nutrition
12. Major congenital malformation (e.g., infants with genetic, metabolic, and/or endocrine disorder diagnosed before enrolment)
13. Intra-uterine growth restriction (IUGR) defined as weight for gestational age less than the third percentile according to Fenton preterm growth chart
14. Confirmed NEC
